title: The Lindberghs homestead
text: August and Louisa Lindbergh settle on 40 acres of woodland east of the future city of Melrose.

title: First convent and school
text: Serving what was then St. Boniface Church; a new convent follows in 1908.

title: Melrose Area Hospital begins
text: Two doctors and a registered nurse open a five-room hospital in a family home on Second Street.

title: The Melrose Theater opens
text: A $50,000, steam-heated, fireproof theater arrives on Main Street. It closed for good in the late 1960s.

title: The Lucky Lady
text: Melrose native Capt. James Gallagher pilots the first non-stop flight around the world.

title: The convent is built
text: A spacious new convent houses 20 sisters — the building that is today's museum.

title: The Society is formed
text: The first museum opens in the basement of the old Lippsmeyer house.

title: A gift from the city
text: The City of Melrose purchases Mary Hall and gives it to the Historical Society.

title: The collection comes home
text: Exhibits move into the renovated, accessible building, with room for a full research center.
